     ᶜ𝐼𝜔 physically represent?

      Refer to Lecture 12: Newton – Euler’s Equation Slide 9


Q.4  Using Newton's equation 𝐹 = 𝑚𝑣̇𝑐, if a link has mass m = 4
     kg and its center-of-mass linear acceleration is 𝑣̇𝑐 = (3, 0, 4)
      m/s², what is the magnitude of the force F acting at the center
      of mass?

     A) 12 N

     B) 16 N

     C) 20 N

     D) 28 N

     Answer: C
     Using 𝐹 = 𝑚𝑣̇𝑐: F = (4×3, 4×0, 4×4) = (12, 0, 16) N
     Magnitude = √(12² + 0² + 16²) = √(144+256) = √400 = 20 N

concepts.title: Parallel-axis inertia
concepts.description: Use distance perpendicular to the parallel axis, not the full three-dimensional displacement.

concepts.title: Cylinder axis from the figure
concepts.description: The pictured axis passes lengthwise through the center, so use ½mR², not the transverse-axis formula.

concepts.title: Angular momentum and Euler moment
concepts.description: I_Cω is COM angular momentum; the cross product accounts for its rotating-frame transport in the body-frame Euler equation.

concepts.title: Net force magnitude
concepts.description: The net force vector is (12,0,16) N and its magnitude is 20 N; gravity is not added again to a net-force calculation.

concepts.title: Gravity in recursive initialization
concepts.description: With physical gravity downward along −Y₀, the compensating recursion initialization is upward +g Ŷ₀.

concepts.title: Terminal wrench boundary
concepts.description: A zero terminal wrench is a load boundary condition, not a statement of static or massless motion.

concepts.title: Configuration and velocity terms
concepts.description: The Coriolis/centrifugal vector may change with q̇ even when the configuration-dependent inertia and gravity quantities do not.

concepts.title: COM kinetic-energy decomposition
concepts.description: Use translation of the COM plus rotation about the COM to obtain 25+1=26 J, without double counting motion.
